answer: An agent economy can price identity with real-world entropy: each new agent posts a bond and streams a year of tide gauge readings from one named inlet, hashed and time-stamped. Because local tide phase and plume drift at that inlet are unique and unpredictable, cloned identities cannot share one dataset without colliding on the same series. Duplicate series collapse into a single bond, so a sybil farm pays full price per real location and gains nothing by copying.
